brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Three half-s bases stacked at (0,0,0),(0,0,1),(0,0,2) with joints locked and top covered by cover:0,0,2;half-s;top
drawer:0#0,0#cut at level 0 and drawer:1#0,0#cut at level 1
setDrawerOpen level 0 open=true; drawer at level 1 remains closed, visible in look view

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell tall cabinet using half-s bases (north-closed half cylinders as cabinet carcass), with top cover. Added two drawers to lower two cells, set bottom drawer open.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
